added_models.model: Ba/F3 cells engineered with MET kinase-domain variants (TPR-MET D1228V; METex14 with ENU-derived secondary mutations) tested against MET TKIs

efficacy.model: Ba/F3 cells engineered with MET kinase-domain variants (TPR-MET D1228V; METex14 with ENU-derived secondary mutations) tested against MET TKIs
efficacy.population: Ba/F3 cells transformed with TPR-MET wild-type or D1228V; 293T MET signalling; PC9 derivatives
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC author manuscript). model_kind is ex_vivo because the enum has no in-vitro cell-line value; the system is an engineered murine pro-B line, not patient cells.
efficacy.note: Ba/F3 cells carrying MET kinase-domain variants first used to ask which MET genotypes lose type I TKI (savolitinib, capmatinib, crizotinib) sensitivity.
efficacy.quote: With several structurally distinct MET inhibitors undergoing development for treatment of NSCLC, it is critical to identify mechanism-based therapies for drug resistance.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the same paper carries the retrodictive comparison, entered separately below.

efficacy.model: Ba/F3 cells engineered with MET kinase-domain variants (TPR-MET D1228V; METex14 with ENU-derived secondary mutations) tested against MET TKIs
efficacy.magnitude_basis: savolitinib sensitivity of TPR-MET wild-type vs D1228V Ba/F3 cells against one patient's progression on savolitinib + osimertinib with a new D1228V mutation
efficacy.population: EGFR-mutant, MET-amplified NSCLC progressing on osimertinib + savolitinib in TATTON (NCT02143466); n = 1
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. Single patient; the D1228V allele was found in the patient first and then engineered into Ba/F3 and 293T cells, so this is a retrodiction. The abstract prints METD1228V with a superscript (quoted here with a space). NCT02143466 has no results posted; savolitinib was given with osimertinib, so the MET-inhibitor resistance is on-target but the response being lost was to a combination.
efficacy.note: Patient's savolitinib + osimertinib resistance mutation D1228V, found by NGS, was modelled: TPR-MET D1228V Ba/F3 cells lost savolitinib sensitivity, reproducing the clinic.
efficacy.short: D1228V savolitinib resistance reproduced in Ba/F3
efficacy.quote: Our in vitro findings demonstrate that MET D1228V induces resistance to type I MET TKIs through impaired drug binding, while sensitivity to type II MET TKIs is maintained.
efficacy.judgement: Scored retro, not same: the clinic already knew the answer (D1228V appeared on savolitinib) before the cells were built (decision 10). The paper's forward prediction, that a type II inhibitor would still work, was tested with cabozantinib, a non-member, so it does not score here. Patient-level because the question is which MET genotype keeps responding.

efficacy.model: Ba/F3 cells engineered with MET kinase-domain variants (TPR-MET D1228V; METex14 with ENU-derived secondary mutations) tested against MET TKIs
efficacy.magnitude_basis: resistance residues named by ENU mutagenesis of Ba/F3 METex14 cells (D1228, Y1230 for type I TKIs) against residues mutated at progression on capmatinib or tepotinib
efficacy.population: METex14 NSCLC progressing on capmatinib or tepotinib (case series and resistance cohorts cited by the source)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Fujino 2019 and Fujino 2022. The 2019 screen's eight TKIs are assumed to include capmatinib and tepotinib (not verifiable from the abstract). Recondo 2020 (10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-19-3608, epub 2020-02-07) reports D1228/Y1230 mutations at progression in 7 of 20 METex14 patients on type I/II MET TKIs but its abstract does not itemise which patients were on member drugs, so the comparison may have been public from 2020; paywalled full text not read.
efficacy.note: ENU mutagenesis of Ba/F3 METex14 (2019) named D1228 and Y1230 as type I resistance sites; both recur at progression on capmatinib and tepotinib.
efficacy.quote: However, the emergence of acquired resistance to capmatinib/tepotinib is almost inevitable partially due to D1228X or Y1230X secondary mutations of the MET.
efficacy.reason: Predicted resistance residues seen on capmatinib/tepotinib
efficacy.judgement: Fresh prospective entry after the 2016 retrodiction (decision 10): the 2019 ENU screen named the type I resistance residues before capmatinib or tepotinib resistance had been characterised in patients, so retrodiction is false, although D1228/Y1230 were already known from crizotinib-treated patients (2016-2017), which a stricter reader would count as partly retrodictive. Direction only: the screen also predicted type II residues (L1195, F1200) that the member drugs, all type I, cannot test.

added_models.model: Patient-derived lung cancer organoids from malignant effusions or tissue, drug-sensitivity tested (LCO-DST) to steer the patient's own next-line therapy

efficacy.model: Patient-derived lung cancer organoids from malignant effusions or tissue, drug-sensitivity tested (LCO-DST) to steer the patient's own next-line therapy
efficacy.population: advanced lung cancer, 212 lung cancer organoids from 107 patients, mostly malignant-effusion derived
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (open access). Earlier lung-adenocarcinoma organoid cohorts (Kim 2021, 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-20-5026) carried no MET-inhibitor case, so the track opens here.
efficacy.note: Lung cancer organoids grown from malignant effusions and drug-sensitivity tested before the next line; first cohort with MET-inhibitor cases.
efficacy.short: Effusion-derived lung organoids built for DST
efficacy.quote: Tumor organoids are a potential approach in precision medicine for predicting the clinical response to treatment.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the same paper carries the comparison, entered separately below.

efficacy.model: Patient-derived lung cancer organoids from malignant effusions or tissue, drug-sensitivity tested (LCO-DST) to steer the patient's own next-line therapy
efficacy.magnitude_basis: organoid IC50 of osimertinib + savolitinib vs either monotherapy against the patient's confirmed partial response; two METex14 cases (P-86, P-105) scored as accurate without the drug named in the main text
efficacy.population: MET-amplified (FISH-confirmed) EGFR L858R NSCLC after EGFR-TKI progression (P-60, n = 1); METex14 NSCLC (P-86, P-105)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. One member-drug case, given as a combination with osimertinib, so the savolitinib contribution is not isolated; the two METex14 cases' drug is in Table S6 (not retrieved) and may be crizotinib rather than a member. Real-world cohort, no registered trial. Cohort-level LCO-DST accuracy (83.3%) is for all targeted and chemotherapy regimens, not MET inhibitors.
efficacy.note: Organoid IC50s picked osimertinib + savolitinib for a MET-amplified EGFR-L858R patient who then had confirmed PR; two METex14 cases also predicted accurately.
efficacy.quote: the patient was given with osimertinib plus savolitinib since MET amplification were further confirmed in MSE and LCO via fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), immunofluorescence staining, and IHC (Figures 5C, 5D, and S5B), and achieved confirmed PR
efficacy.reason: Organoid call matched the patient's response
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level, prospective (the organoid test preceded the treatment choice), stated in the source. Scored same on one member-drug patient; a reader who requires the MET inhibitor to be given alone, or more than one patient, would leave this untested.

dose.model: Quantitative systems pharmacology model of the MET signalling network with virtual METex14 and MET-amplified NSCLC populations run as virtual clinical trials
dose.population: virtual METex14 NSCLC population (5,000 virtual patients)
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (open access). The paper's typo 'savoltinib' is kept verbatim in the quote.
dose.note: Virtual trials across doses: approved capmatinib and tepotinib doses near-optimal for ORR, savolitinib efficacy plateaus near 500 mg; no patient dose comparison.
dose.quote: the clinically approved dose for tepotinib, capmatinib and crizotinib was rather optimal, while for savoltinib similar efficacy can be achieved at lower doses
dose.judgement: A dose prediction exists (lower savolitinib dose equivalent) but no trial has tested it, so untested rather than an empty cell.

efficacy.model: Quantitative systems pharmacology model of the MET signalling network with virtual METex14 and MET-amplified NSCLC populations run as virtual clinical trials
efficacy.population: ODE model (about 130 species, 69 equations, PK modules for 16 drugs) calibrated on MET-aberrant cell lines and xenografts
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (open access). Built in 2025, after every member trial it is compared with had read out.
efficacy.note: First QSP model of MET signalling; calibrated on capmatinib, tepotinib and savolitinib cell and xenograft data before any clinical comparison.
efficacy.short: MET QSP model built from preclinical data
efficacy.quote: To our knowledge, our work is the first multiscale QSP investigation of MET dysregulation for translational cancer drug research
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the retrodictive virtual-trial comparison in the same paper is entered separately below.

efficacy.model: Quantitative systems pharmacology model of the MET signalling network with virtual METex14 and MET-amplified NSCLC populations run as virtual clinical trials
efficacy.magnitude_basis: simulated vs reported ORR and waterfall response depth (Figure 6I table; the paper's numbers were not extracted, so no fold is computed)
efficacy.population: METex14 NSCLC (GEOMETRY mono-1, VISION, savolitinib NCT02897479) and MET-amplified NSCLC (GEOMETRY mono-1)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. Capmatinib, tepotinib and crizotinib clinical responses were the training set for the virtual METex14 population, so only the savolitinib (Lu 2021) and MET-amplified capmatinib comparisons are out of sample; the match is the authors' own, judged on waterfall overlap and ORR.
efficacy.note: Virtual trials reproduced GEOMETRY and VISION ORRs after training, then matched savolitinib's METex14 ORR and capmatinib's lower MET-amplified ORR out of sample.
efficacy.quote: the resulting predicted treatment response can again match the reported clinical data in MET ex14 mutated NSCLC patients
efficacy.judgement: Retro, not same: every trial compared had read out (2020-2021) before the model was built (decision 10). Class-level because the virtual populations ask whether MET TKIs work in METex14 or MET-amplified NSCLC as a whole. The PDO arm of the same paper tested no member drug and reports no patient outcome, so it adds nothing to this track.

patient_trials.quote: Capmatinib showed substantial antitumor activity in patients with advanced NSCLC with a MET exon 14 skipping mutation, particularly in those not treated previously.
Among patients with advanced NSCLC with a confirmed MET exon 14 skipping mutation, the use of tepotinib was associated with a partial response in approximately half the patients.
Savolitinib yielded promising activity and had an acceptable safety profile in patients with pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma and other NSCLC subtypes positive for METex14 skipping alterations.

considered_not_added: Lu 2017 immunocompetent MetDelta15/Trp53-flox mouse (10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-16-1944): the only inhibitor dosed in the model was crizotinib (50 mg/kg, non-member) and the paired patient was also on crizotinib; 'Met inhibition showed clinical benefit in this model' is crizotinib in the full text, so no member-drug prediction exists and it is note-only.

Fernandes 2023 CRISPR METex14 16HBE cells in humanised-HGF knock-in NSG mice (10.1002/1878-0261.13397): in-vivo TKIs were crizotinib and OMO-1 (non-members); capmatinib was used only in vitro on the isogenic cells; VISION and GEOMETRY ORRs are cited in the introduction, not compared with a model result. No member-drug in-vivo retrodiction to score.

Ai 2018 gumarontinib/SCC244 NSCLC PDX (10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-17-0368) and Gavine 2015 savolitinib gastric PDX (10.1016/j.molonc.2014.08.015): MET-driven xenografts in immunodeficient mice, the same system and the same prediction as the draft's met-driven-xenograft track; they belong on that track, not a new one.

Hu 2025 patient-derived-organoid arm (10.3389/fphar.2025.1685468): organoids from 5 MET-amplified NSCLC patients were tested with erlotinib, sorafenib, regorafenib, afatinib, cabozantinib, donafenib, gefitinib, lapatinib, crizotinib, futibatinib and chemotherapy, no member drug, and the paper reports no outcome for those patients; only the QSP virtual-trial arm is added.

Kim 2021 advanced lung adenocarcinoma organoids (10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-20-5026, full text read): 10 MET-amplified organoids but every organoid-vs-patient comparison is an EGFR- or BRAF-directed therapy; no MET-inhibitor case, so it cannot open the organoid track earlier than 2023.

Recondo 2020 resistance series (10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-19-3608): patient-side only; the abstract does not say which of the 20 METex14 patients were on capmatinib, tepotinib or savolitinib, and the full text is paywalled, so it was not used to date the Ba/F3 comparison to 2020 (flagged in that entry).

Rotow 2019 (10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-19-1667): ctDNA landscape with a METex14 cell model of RAS-MAPK co-alteration resistance; the model was dosed with crizotinib and the patients' MET-TKI mix is not itemised, so no member-drug comparison.

HGF-transgenic mice bearing EGFR-mutant HCC827/PC9 tumours in the FDA tepotinib review (no tepotinib effect despite MET activation): a negative-selection datum from the same xenograft-in-mouse system as the met-driven-xenograft track, not a new system.
Capmatinib and tepotinib PBPK models in the FDA reviews: used for drug-interaction predictions only, never compared with an efficacy or dose-target result in patients; not a track.

GEOMETRY-III (NCT04427072) and VISION cohort B (Le 2023, 10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101280): patient-side items for the existing met-driven-xenograft efficacy entry's patient_trials, outside the scope of added_models.
